sāriputta.notes: MN 24 identifies Upatissa as Sāriputta in his own words, and AN 1.189 singles him out for wisdom. Several citations span neighboring discourses. For example, MN 23 concerns Kumārakassapa, while the exchange with Puṇṇa is in MN 24.

sātāgira.notes: Snp 1.9 explicitly labels the speaker sātāgiro yakkho. The entry describes him and mentions the mountain as his birthplace.

sāvitti.notes: Snp 3.4 describes the prayer as three lines of twenty-four syllables. The entry prints chandato mukhaṁ where Snp 3.7 and MN 92 read chandaso mukhaṁ.

sīha.notes: The three AN texts call Sīha senāpati. AN 5.33 and AN 8.11 are adjacent citation hits. DN 6 calls Nāgita’s messenger a novice. Thag 1.83 attributes its verse to Sīha Thera, for whom the packet supplies no entry. Thig 5.3 names the nun Sīhā.

sītavana.notes: AN 6.55 places Soṇa in the Cool Grove at Rājagaha. The cited episodes of Anāthapiṇḍika and Upasena occur in SN 10.8 and SN 35.69. SN 10.7 and SN 35.68 are neighboring discourses. Thag 10.2 mentions a cool grove without naming the city.

sīvaka.notes: SN 10.8 and DN 32 spell the yakkha’s name Sivako, which opens the short-i dictionary senses. Thag 1.14 addresses Vanavaccha’s novice, and the chapter summary at Thag 1.20 lists him after Vanavaccha. DPD assigns sīvaka 2 to the elder of Thag 2.32, a different verse attribution. AN 6.47 and SN 36.21 address the wanderer Moḷiyasīvaka.

sūra.notes: DN 32 lists Sūra among Kuvera’s messengers. Snp 4.8 addresses the debater called Pasūra later in the same poem.

tacchakā.notes: DN 20.11.2 includes the nāgas in sahatacchakā. DPD gives this compound its own line, and Sujato renders the group as those from Takkasilā. This accounts for the empty mention list.

tagarasikhī.notes: SN 3.20 tells the entry’s almsgiving episode. The Pāli spells the name taggarasikhiṁ there, which opens the separate taggarasikhī lemma.

tavakaṇṇika.notes: AN 6.120–139 names Tavakaṇṇika as a householder. AN 6.119 concerns Tapussa, and AN 6.140 begins the abbreviated texts on greed.

taṇhā.notes: SN 4.25 explicitly calls Taṇhā a daughter of Māra, and Snp 4.9 opens by naming her with Arati and Ragā. Sujato translates her name as Craving in both, so the English name filter misses them. SN 4.24 and Snp 4.8 are adjacent citation hits.

tikaṇṇa.notes: In the app the conversation is AN 3.58. AN 3.59, the DPD hint, names Jāṇussoṇi. AN 3.60 includes Tikaṇṇa in its closing chapter summary. DPPN cites DN 2 for comparison with the teaching on the three knowledges.

timbaruka.notes: SN 12.18 contains Timbaruka’s questions on pleasure and pain. The citation lands in SN 12.17, where Kassapa the naked ascetic asks the questions. SN 12.20 names Timbaruka in the chapter summary.

tissa.notes: In DN 14 the taps on Tissa identify Vipassī’s disciple, the high priest’s son in the city of Bandhumatī. Kassapa’s disciple also appears at DN 14:1.9.6, inside the separately defined compound tissabhāradvājaṁ. Thag 10.2 credits Ekavihāriya, the elder whose verses Tissa 22 cites. The name Tissa and the identification as Asoka’s brother come from the biographical tradition. DN 20 lists Tissa among divinities but gives no detail linking him to the reborn monk visited by Moggallāna. AN 6.32–33, SN 21.10 and SN 22.83 are neighboring citation hits. Snp 4.7 names Tissametteyya. AN 8.91–117 and Thig 1.4–5 concern women named Tissā.

tissā.notes: AN 8.91–117 lists the laywoman beside Tissamātā. AN 8.118–119 begin a series on greed. Thig 1.4 and 1.5 attribute their verses to two nuns named Tissā. The AN 6.34, DN 14, SN 21.9 and SN 22.84 hits come from forms shared with masculine Tissa.

tivarā.notes: SN 15.20 names the people, their lifespan and the mountain. SN 15.18 and SN 15.19 are adjacent citation hits.

todeyya.notes: MN 99 explicitly names Subha’s father among the prominent brahmins. AN 4.187 recounts the discussion of Eḷeyya in Todeyya’s assembly. MN 100, DPD’s example, uses the plural todeyyānaṁ brāhmaṇānaṁ for the owners of a grove. SN 35.133 names one brahmin Todeyya as the owner of the Kāmaṇḍā grove, but neither the sutta nor DPPN establishes his identity with Subha’s father. SN 35.132 concerns Lohicca. The three Pārāyana texts identify Bāvarī’s pupil by his companions or his questions.

tuṭṭha.notes: DN 16 and SN 55.10 name the deceased lay follower. SN 55.9 gives a different list of disciples at Ñātika.

tālapuṭa.notes: Both DPD senses cite SN 42.2. The closing passage follows the same dancing chief through ordination and awakening, so both lines describe the person in this entry. SN 42.1 concerns Caṇḍa.
